roster.name: Zarya + Zvezda
roster.note: the first two modules — a US-funded, Russian-built control module (1998) and the Russian service module (2000) that made the station habitable; the marriage of the two former rivals' station heritage

roster.name: Expedition 1
roster.note: the first resident crew arrived on 2 November 2000; humans have lived aboard continuously ever since — the longest unbroken human presence off Earth in history

roster.name: Columbus + Kibo
roster.note: the European and Japanese laboratories, which turned the station into a genuinely global facility with modules from five space agencies

roster.name: Commercial Crew
roster.note: SpaceX's Crew Dragon restored US crew launch after nine years of dependence on Soyuz, and began the handover of low-orbit access to commercial providers

see_also.label: Mir — the station the ISS inherited from
